clusters.title: Install and run a service package
clusters.reasoning: These adjacent concepts are complementary steps in preparing a runnable Python service: reconstruct its declared dependencies and organize and execute its importable package. Both require only the isolated-environment foundation already available at tile start. Dependency installation and package identity retain separate sub-concepts and exercises; neither is presented as a substitute for the other.

clusters.title: Compose validated request models
clusters.reasoning: Field constraints and nested models are complementary parts of declaring a validated request-data structure. Both build on model construction and type annotations already available at tile start. Keep value restrictions and structural composition as separate, ordered sub-concepts rather than implying that either declaration replaces the other.

clusters.title: Declare and inspect an input contract
clusters.reasoning: Input presence, nullability and defaults describe the accepted input contract; OpenAPI generation supplies its inspectable public description. These adjacent concepts fit a declaration-and-inspection workflow, and both have their prerequisites before the tile. Keep executable input behavior distinct from generated documentation, and retain the separate absence, null and concrete-value cases.

clusters.title: Bind and validate request metadata
clusters.reasoning: Header and cookie binding and request-validation errors fit the workflow of declaring metadata inputs and checking invalid request outcomes. All prerequisites for both are already available at tile start. Separate source/name binding from validation failure handling, and preserve the distinction between invalid client input and server-side validation bugs.

clusters.title: Preserve input intent as contracts evolve
clusters.reasoning: Partial-update extraction and compatible contract changes share the problem of preserving what a client request means. Both can be learned from prerequisites already completed before this tile. Keep omitted fields versus explicit null visible in the update sub-concept, and keep compatibility review as its own broader contract check rather than treating partial-update extraction as proof of compatibility.

clusters.title: Translate and format public API errors
clusters.reasoning: The adjacent error-translation and error-envelope concepts are complementary parts of turning recognized internal failures into stable public HTTP responses. Both have all prerequisites at tile start; the earlier model-boundary concept in this tile is not needed by either. Keep choosing an intentional HTTP outcome separate from formatting its body, preserving status, relevant headers and transaction recovery rather than allowing a uniform envelope to erase those boundaries.

clusters.title: Commit and verify ORM resource mutations
clusters.reasoning: Creation, deletion and update are variants of one ORM resource-mutation workflow: change mapped state, complete the transaction and verify the durable result independently. Each concept has all prerequisites before the tile, so none needs another mutation introduced here. Preserve TOC order and separate operation labels: creation verifies stored identity and fields, deletion verifies absence, and update verifies changed and preserved fields. The shared explanation does not merge their bundles or exercises.

clusters.title: Keep cache-backed reads correct
clusters.reasoning: Freshness and safe cache failure are complementary policies for the already-learned cache-aside read. Both have all prerequisites at tile start. Separate stale-data control through expiry and write invalidation from unavailable-cache handling through bounded waits and primary-store fallback; an expiry policy is not an outage policy, and a fallback does not establish freshness of an existing cached copy.
